**Date:** {{< meta display-date >}}  
**From:** {{< meta from-address >}}  
**Manuscript Location:** {{< meta manuscript-location >}}  

Madam
I was in hopes of being able to tell you of such a training ship as you desire, knowing that there was one under the management in part of a [Mr Chambers](../persons.html#2074), an excellent Churchman but I find that is a Reformatory Ship and that I suppose would hardly be what you wish, but if you would like further enquiries to be made, I could procure Mr Chambers address.[^1]

Yours truly

C M Yonge (Ed [M P](../others.html#52))

[^1]: MP (January 1865) \'Notices to Correspondents\' noted \'A Subscriber may be glad to know that funds are being raised to establish a training ship in the Mersey for good destitute boys, on a similar plan to the Akbar Reformatory Ship.

Treasurer, John Clint Esq., Liverpool.’ George H.

Chambers was chairman of the committee of the training ship Worcester (The Times 29 September 1874).
